column1: # THE ANCIENTS, DRESSED PER FACE -- R275 (2026-09-17).
# One row per (Ancient, face); `tools/gen_teyvat_ancients.py` reads this file
# and the decompiled facts behind it are `docs/current/operations/codegen.md`,
# EVERY TEXT COLUMN MAY BE EMPTY AND TODAY EVERY ONE OF THEM IS. An empty cell
# means KEEP THE GAME'S OWN LINE: `TeyvatLoc.Inject` copies the live row from
# the base Ancient's key onto the dressed key before laying the face's own
# rows over the top, so a name-only pass ships with the game's words intact,
# in every language, with no base-game prose in this repo. Filling a cell in
#   ancient      the base Ancient's Id.Entry (NEOW, OROBAS, PAEL, TEZCATARA,
#   name         REQUIRED. The dressed name. The C# class, the Id.Entry, the
#                title row and every asset path derive from it.
#   epithet      the line under the name on the banner (`<ENTRY>.epithet`)
#   first_visit  the once-ever dialogue, shown the first time ANY character
#                meets this Ancient. Lines separated by `|`, each line
#                character speaks). The line COUNT is fixed by compiled C#
#                the per-character dialogues at visit 0, visit 1 and visit 4.
#                NOTHING IN OUR ROSTER READS THESE: `CharacterDialogues` is
#                Kokomi and Furina miss the lookup and fall through to the
#                agnostic list. Written per character when they are written:
#   agnostic_1   the ANY-character dialogue 0 -- what a Teyvat run reads.
#   agnostic_2   every REMAINING ANY dialogue, `;;`-separated in index order.
#                Two for most Ancients, three for Vakuu, five for Neow.
#   extra        flat rows under the dressed entry, `key= text ;; key= text`.
#                This is where Neow's `results.prefix`, Vakuu's `loss` and
#                go when a face wants to restate them.
# NO BOON IS WRITTEN HERE, EVER. An Ancient's options are RelicOption<T>() and
# `EventOption.FromRelic` falls through to the relic's own rows when the event
# has none, so the boon a player reads is the game's whatever this file says.

column5: A: Oh, a climber! Let me find my notes. I have been meaning to add a chapter on this place, and you look like the kind of footnote that survives.
column9: A: If you meet a small girl with a backpack full of bombs, tell her Mother says to do her homework. Now, what does the Travel Guide recommend for someone in your position?
column10: A: The Fontaine chapter is mostly notes on the courthouse, which I recommend viewing from outside. Choose from the parts that got me arrested.

column10: A: The Akademiya banned the Travel Guide, which doubled its sales. Here is a page they especially hated.

column5: A: Hm. A mortal at the foot of the mountain, and the tea not yet cool. Very well. Choose your provision.
column9: A: The adepti keep a contract with Liyue, and I keep mine with any who climb. Choose, then.
column10: A: Mt. Aocang has watched a thousand ascents. Most were foolish. Some were not. Which are you? ;; A: Do not thank me. A gift given at the foot of a climb is only the mountain's toll paid forward. ;; A: I have sat still for centuries and learned little. Perhaps motion teaches better. Go and see. ;; A: Rex Lapis is gone, and still the contracts hold. Here is mine: one gift, then the road.

column5: A: You carry the scent of the wind that woke me. Take what a wounded sky can spare, and go.
column9: A: The storm has passed over Mondstadt, and I remain. Choose, traveler, before the wind changes.
column10: A: Once I feared every hand that reached for me. Reach anyway. The choice is yours to make. ;; A: The Spire is not the sky, but it climbs the same way. Take your first breath of it here. ;; A: I have lain beneath Stormterror's Lair long enough to know a beginning when it walks in. ;; A: A dragon's gift is a small wind at your back. It is all I have, and it is enough.

column5: A: Every river in Fontaine began as a gift I was not permitted to give. I give it anyway. Take your share.
column9: A: Abundance was my sin and my reason. Let some of it fall on you before the judgment falls on me.
column10: A: My Melusines were born from a giant's tears. From what shall your fortune be born? Choose.

column5: A: The forest remembers what the city forgot. Come. What grows here grows for everyone who climbs.
column9: A: Wisdom is not withheld, only offered to those who arrive. You have arrived. Take what the branches carry.
column10: A: I gave away everything, even my name, so the forest might keep growing. One more gift will not hurt.

column5: A: The petals fall and I remain. Lay your burden at my roots; what you hold will leave stronger than it came.
column9: A: The shrine is quiet tonight. Set down what you carry, and let the roots refine it.
column10: A: A blade is polished a thousand times before it is trusted. Your thousand times begin here.

column5: A: The flame does not care what you were. It cares what you become. Show me what you carry, and I will make it burn hotter.
column9: A: A warrior who stops sharpening is already dead. Give me your blade.
column10: A: Natlan was not built by the strong. It was built by those who kept fighting after strength ran out.

column5: A: I chose my ending long ago, beneath Yashiori. Whatever remains of me is yours, if you can carry it.
column9: A: The Tatarigami whisper that a god should keep what is his. I never listened. Take what you need.
column10: A: Watatsumi still eats because I stopped breathing. Let a little of that bargain feed you as well.

column5: A: The Night Kingdom is claiming me, piece by piece. Before it takes the last, let me give some of it to you.
column9: A: A dragon does not die all at once. Take a piece of me, then, and make it count.
column10: A: My scales bought Natlan its dawn. One more will buy you yours.

column5: A: I dreamed of the sea before Fontaine had a name. Come, little one. The dreaming body has strength to spare.
column9: A: The Melusines grew from my wounds. So can you. Take from me, and be whole.
column10: A: They tell me I fell from the sky. I only remember the ground, and the small ones who tended it. Let me tend you.

column5: A: The sands have swallowed kingdoms, and I have swallowed the sands. What is one more mortal, taken in and returned stronger?
column9: A: Enter, mortal. Nothing that passes through me leaves unchanged.
column10: A: Deshret tried to build a paradise on my back. You want only a boon. That much I can grant.

column5: A: Ha! A guest who did not get lost in my forest. That deserves a drink. Or a meal. Or both. Pick.
column9: A: The kitsune host with ceremony. We tanuki host with sake. Choose whichever you find on the table.
column10: A: Nothing in Chinju Forest is what it seems, except the food. The food is real. Eat.

column4: A Wayob of the Night Kingdom
column5: A: Sit. Eat. The Night Kingdom has long tables and few guests, and you look like one who forgets to rest.
column9: A: Hospitality is the oldest law of the tribes. Take a seat by the fire, and take something for the road.
column10: A: The living pass through the Night Kingdom too quickly to taste anything. You will not make that mistake.

column5: A: Every gift I gave Remuria carried a debt. None of them refused. Will you?
column9: A: Power arrives with its price already written. Read the terms, then sign.
column10: A: I raised a golden city on borrowed harmony, and the sea collected. Choose carefully what you borrow. ;; A: The symphony was worth the drowning. I still believe that. Perhaps you will believe it too.

column5: A: I sought forbidden knowledge and paid for it with my kingdom. Take a smaller lesson. It still costs.
column9: A: The desert keeps every bargain. So do I. Choose what you will give up.
column10: A: Gurabad, Ay-Khanoum, Sabzeruz. Names of things I bought too dearly. Buy something smaller from me. ;; A: Knowledge is never free. The Eremites learned that from my sands. You will learn it here.
